question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.**

Getting the long-awaited promotion is a/an **__milestone__** in her career.
solution:
The correct answer is** "Important event."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom** "milestone"** refers to a significant event or achievement in one's life or career. (किसी के जीवन या करियर में एक महत्वपूर्ण घटना या उपलब्धि)
 
• In this context,** "getting the long-awaited promotion"** is a milestone because it marks a major accomplishment in the woman's career.
 
• The word** "milestone"** is often used metaphorically to refer to important events or achievements, such as graduating from college or buying a house.
 
 
• **Example**:* Learning to walk is a **milestone**__ in a child's development.*
 
 
 
• Grammatically, **"milestone"** is a noun that functions as the subject of the sentence.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2 .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 -** Burden**: A **"burden"** refers to something that is heavy or difficult to bear. (बोझा, वज़न)
 
• Option 3 - **Wonder**:** "Wonder"** refers to a feeling of surprise or amazement. (आश्‍चर्य और आदर का भाव)
 
• Option 4 - **Mishap**: A **"mishap"** refers to an unfortunate or unlucky event. (मामूली दुर्घटना या अशुभ प्रसंग)
